newsitem.title: INDIA: India arrests Kashmiri militant for blasts.
newsitem.headline: India arrests Kashmiri militant for blasts.

text.p: Indian police have arrested the leader of a hardline Kashmiri separatist group responsible for three bomb blasts in the state of Jammu and Kashmir, police said on Monday.

"Supreme commander of Jamiat-ul-Mujahideen (JUM), Ghulam Rasool Shah, and his associate, responsible for three major blasts, were arrested by Special Operations Group of Jammu and Kashmir police on June 19," state police chief Gurbachan Jagat told a news conference.

The Special Operations Group is a counter-insurgency wing of the police in Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority province, where seven years of separatist rebellion have killed more than 20,000 people.
Most streets in Srinagar were deserted on Monday as a result of a general strike called by JUM to protest against the arrest of its leader.
JUM has claimed responsibility for an unsuccessful bombing attack on state chief minister Farooq Abdullah last September as he was about to arrive at a graveyard where his father was buried.
The group also owned up to another blast near the chief minister's home on January 3 in which eight people were killed.
JUM said it was behind a car bomb that killed two policemen last October near a tightly-guarded hostel for state lawmakers elected in local polls that were the first to be held for nine years.

"We have almost wiped out JUM with the arrest of its top leadership," Jagat said. "They were directed by ISI (Inter Service Intelligence of Pakistan) to target MLAs (members of legislative assemblies) and ministers," he said.
India accuses Pakistan of arming Kashmiri militants, but Islamabad says it provides only political and diplomatic support to separatists seeking independence or merger with Pakistan.
